name: Higashi-Ginza
tagline: Toranomon in 6 minutes and Tokyo in 9 minutes. Served by 2 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥160,000 to ¥170,000.
summary: The station is in Chuo City, served by Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line and Toei Asakusa Line. Journey times to the main business districts are 10 minutes to Otemachi, 22 minutes to Shinjuku, 22 minutes to Shibuya and 14 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥160,000 to ¥170,000. The station stands 2.9 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 1.9 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 2.9 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 2.1 m to 4 m, a difference of 1.9 m. These figures were read from the elevation API of the Geospatial Information Authority of Japan at nine points: the station itself and eight compass directions 400 m out.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 7 fall inside the area, and the deepest projection among them is 0.5 to 3 m. For storm surge, 3 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. The projected depth differs block by block within the same station area, so check the ward hazard map for the specific address. Inland flooding from overwhelmed drains has no nationwide map; each ward publishes its own, and that is worth reading as well.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 13 clinics and 8 pharmacies. Facilities recorded as hospitals lie at 国立がん研究センター中央病院, about 465 m away and 十仁病院, about 783 m away. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station: Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line and Toei Asakusa Line. The lines are split between operators (Tokyo Metro runs 1 line and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company. Scored out of 100 from the number of lines and the spread of operators, transfer convenience here comes to 57.

rentRange.note: One room ¥160,000 to ¥170,000, 1K ¥140,000 to ¥150,000, 1LDK ¥240,000 to ¥250,000 and 2LDK ¥330,000 to ¥340,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥160,000 to ¥170,000. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: rents are lower at Higashi-Ginza, but Ginza is ahead on the number of lines and how little of the area is in the flood projection.
neighbours.note: 414 m away in a straight line. It reaches Otemachi 6 minutes sooner than Higashi-Ginza. One-room rents run about ¥10,000 higher.

neighbours.lead: rents are lower at Tsukijishijo, but Higashi-Ginza is ahead on the number of lines and how close the centre is.
neighbours.note: 508 m away in a straight line. It takes 11 minutes longer to reach Otemachi than Higashi-Ginza. One-room rents run about ¥14,000 lower.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who get around by bicycle or with a pushchair
notFor: People avoiding projected flood inundation areas
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
People who want to hold the rent down
noiseSources: The 首都高速都心環状線 viaduct runs 162 m away. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
晴海通り (3 lanes each way) runs 3 m away, right beside the station. Traffic on it never stops

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 1 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 9 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The number of points that fall inside the projected inundation area is about average for a station in the 23 wards.
leads.stationNote: 2 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the low side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
leads.noiseSources: At this station, check the traffic noise before the noise people make: 首都高速都心環状線 runs 162 m away.
